subject: FastCart discovery — tenant controls, quotas, and routing plan
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@fastcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & proposed next steps from today's discovery

Hi Elaine — thanks for your time today. Quick write-up to capture what we heard and confirm next steps.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: unpredictable per-customer costs and noisy tenants causing latency spikes for high-value customers.
- Desired outcomes: per-tenant rate controls, tiered QoS routing, and a predictable quota model tied to SLAs.

What we heard (pain points)
- FastCart has several high-volume customers where a small percentage of bad requests causes upstream tail latency; you need per-customer throttling and automatic isolation.
- Current stack: internal gateway -> Kubernetes-hosted model endpoints (self-hosted) with a mix of on-demand GPUs (EC2) and some inference cached on Redis. No consistent per-tenant enforcement today.
- Cost unpredictability: spikes from a few tenants lead to large monthly overage and make forecasting hard.
- Compliance note: logs and auditability are required for your enterprise customers (SOC2-like evidence).

Success criteria (what will make this a win)
- Ability to define per-customer quotas (tokens/day and concurrency limits) and enforce them with minimal latency delta (+<15ms p50 target).
- Tiering: bronze/silver/gold routing so Gold customers get lower queueing and reserved throughput.
- Transparent billing: per-tenant cost breakdown + forecastable commit option.
- Auditability: request-level logs for last 90 days with export capability.

Possible Redwood fit (high level)
- Dedicated tenant routing and per-customer quotas via policy profiles.
- Prefix/KV cache to reduce tokens on repeat queries for lower tiers.
- Canary routing rules for tiered fallback in overload.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Ben (solutions engineer) — we recommend 45–60m to review architecture, realistic latency numbers, and a small pilot plan. (Owner: Ben Carter)
2) Draft a mutual action plan (MAP) including success metrics and timeline; I can put a first-pass MAP in Drive. (Owner: Nikhil Sharma)
3) Procurement touchpoint — Elaine to share procurement contact / timing if you want a committed pricing path.

Can you confirm above and share availability for a technical follow-up? Also, if there are any other stakeholders (security, infra, procurement) who should join, include them.

Thanks again — next step suggestion: Ben + Elaine on Wed or Thu next week.

Best,
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma

Thanks Nikhil — this is a great summary and aligns with our notes. A few clarifications and priorities from our side: 

Priorities (ranked)
1) Per-customer concurrency controls and graceful degradation for gold customers (must-have).
2) Clear quota definitions + billing visibility (want).
3) Audit logs retained 90 days, exportable to our S3 (must-have for procurement).

Technical constraints
- We cannot introduce a significant new proxy hop in the request path; any enforcement should ideally live at the model ingress or be implemented via lightweight routing layer.
- We use AWS EKS and have a strict IAM policy — if you need cross-account roles, procurement will need to review.

Procurement note
- CC'ing Tom Riley (our procurement lead) — Tom, we are evaluating Redwood as a vendor for inference serving and this thread has the initial technical/商业 scope. Could you provide procurement windows and any standard documents you need?

Availability
- Ben: Wed 24 Feb 10:00–11:00 PT / Thu 25 Feb 14:00–15:00 PT both work for the technical deep-dive.

Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Engineering, FastCart
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Recap & proposed next steps from today's discovery

Elaine — thanks for the clear priorities. A few technical notes ahead of the deep-dive to make the session productive: 

Quick feasibility points
- Enforcement locations: we can offer per-tenant controls at the routing layer (fast, config-driven) or at the model server level (stronger guarantees). Given the "no proxy hop" constraint, we suggest integrating our lightweight routing library as a sidecar or as a small routing layer co-located with your ingress — minimal added latency in our tests (~6–12ms p50).
- Quota units: we recommend a hybrid quota (tokens/day for billing, concurrency windows for burst protection).
- Audit logs: Redwood can ship request-level events to customer S3 with TLS and KMS-encrypted payloads; retention policy configurable.

Attachments: attaching a short options deck and a sample MAP spreadsheet with suggested milestones.
(attachment: redwood-tenant-controls-options.pdf)
(attachment: fastcart-map.xlsx)

Proposed agenda for the 45m deep-dive
- 0–10m: confirm FastCart current flow and constraints (you lead)
- 10–25m: configuration options (per-tenant quotas, concurrency, reserved throughput)
- 25–35m: demo of routing sidecar and policy UI (Ben)
- 35–45m: agree pilot scope and success metrics (MAP next steps)

If you want, I can include a quick cost forecast for a 3-month pilot ahead of the call.

Ben Carter
